req.title: Delete unknown returns 404
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 404 when DELETE targets a non-existent task id.

doc.reasoning: R-TASK-014 requires that DELETE /tasks/{task_id} returns HTTP 404 when the task_id does not exist. To achieve high mutation kill rate we need: (1) a positive case confirming a known-existing task can be deleted with 204, (2) a negative case confirming a clearly non-existent id returns exactly 404 with the correct detail message, (3) a boundary case at id=21 (one beyond the highest seeded id=20) to catch off-by-one mutations, (4) a boundary case at id=0 (below the minimum valid id) to catch boundary mutations, and (5) a state-transition case confirming that deleting an already-deleted task returns 404 on the second call. All tests use in-process FastAPI TestClient with a fresh SQLite in-memory database seeded with the specified rows, ensuring determinism and idempotency.

tests.name: test_delete_existing_task_returns_204
preconditions: Database contains task with id=1 (Read chapter 5, completed=true)
FastAPI app is running in-process via TestClient
trace: R-TASK-014: confirms the happy-path complement — existing task deleted successfully, establishing baseline before testing 404 path
tests.executable:
import os, tempfile
from sqlalchemy import create_engine
from sqlalchemy.orm import sessionmaker
from app.main import app
from app import models
from app.database import get_db
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

def test_delete_existing_task_returns_204():
    db_fd, db_path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.db')
    os.close(db_fd)
    engine = create_engine(f'sqlite:///{db_path}', connect_args={'check_same_thread': False})
    models.Base.metadata.create_all(bind=engine)
    Session = sessionmaker(bind=engine)
    db = Session()
    db.add(models.Task(id=1, title='Read chapter 5', description='desc', completed=True))
    db.commit()
    db.close()
    def override_get_db():
        s = Session()
        try:
            yield s
        finally:
            s.close()
    app.dependency_overrides[get_db] = override_get_db
    client = TestClient(app)
    r = client.delete('/tasks/1')
    assert r.status_code == 204
    assert r.content == b''
    app.dependency_overrides.clear()
    os.unlink(db_path)

test_delete_existing_task_returns_204()

tests.name: test_delete_already_deleted_task_returns_404
preconditions: Database contains task with id=5 (Write project report)
Task id=5 is successfully deleted in first DELETE call
actions: Send DELETE /tasks/5 (first call — task exists, expect 204)
Send DELETE /tasks/5 (second call — task no longer exists, expect 404)
expected: Second DELETE response JSON detail equals 'Task with id 5 not found'
trace: R-TASK-014: STC — state transition from 'task exists' to 'task deleted'; second delete must return 404, catching mutations that skip the not-found guard

from sqlalchemy import create_engine
from sqlalchemy.orm import sessionmaker
from app.main import app

from app.database import get_db
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

def test_delete_already_deleted_task_returns_404():
    db_fd, db_path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.db')
